title: Study of a two species microbial community by an inferential comparative genomic analysis tool: Spatial Analytical Microbial Imaging
author: Zhang, Valverde, et al.
materials: 1In both 2D and 3D data analysis, channels were split, thresholds were set to enclose most data point in a narrow range. The values, such as mean value, geometric center, binding area, were analyzed based on the original imaging data acquired by LSM 510 software and the results displayed.2Do the same process to mixed samples and concurrently grown pure cultures and the slow growth pure cultures.3Compare the average fluorescence intensity (AFI) of each cell in mixed culture to the mean value of the pure culture and differentiate the cells in the mixed culture.4Plot identified results using 3D data (x, y, z) in sigmaplot 10.0 and compare with the control (Fig. 1).5Compare the GFA of the identified cells in the mixed culture with that of the slow growth pure culture standard to evaluate the relative genomic copy number of each cell and identify their 3D locus in the mixture (Fig. 2).

steps.title: Prepare mixed-species culture on slide
steps.instruction: Grow a pure culture of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 on a glass slide under room light and room temperature (27 °C ± 1 °C).

steps.title: Add E. coli suspension to slide
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of pure‑culture E. coli K‑12 MG1655 suspension onto the Synechocystis‑covered slide (Phase I).

steps.title: Feed culture with BG‑11 media
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of BG‑11 medium to the slide each day for three consecutive days (Phase II).

steps.title: Incubate mixed culture
steps.instruction: Incubate the slide at room temperature (27 °C ± 1 °C) for an additional three days (Phase III).

steps.title: Prepare pure‑culture controls
steps.instruction: Simultaneously prepare pure‑culture standards of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 and E. coli K‑12 MG1655 to serve as controls.

steps.title: Prepare slow‑growth E. coli standard
steps.instruction: Obtain a slow‑growth E. coli K‑12 MG1655 culture by serial dilution.

substeps.instruction: Isolate a single colony from an LB agar plate.
Inoculate the colony into 10 mL M9 medium.
Incubate in a shaker at 27 °C ± 1 °C for 3 days.
Transfer 1 mL of this culture into 10 mL fresh M9 medium and incubate under the same conditions for another 3 days.
Repeat the 1 mL → 10 mL transfer (serial dilution) at least three times to obtain the slow‑growth standard.

steps.title: Prepare slow‑growth Synechocystis standard
steps.instruction: Obtain a slow‑growth Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 culture by serial dilution.

substeps.instruction: Isolate a single colony of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803.
Grow the colony in 10 mL BG‑11 medium for 3 days under room light and 27 °C ± 1 °C.
Transfer 1 mL of this culture into 10 mL fresh BG‑11 medium and grow for another 3 days under the same conditions.
Repeat the 1 mL → 10 mL transfer at least three times.

steps.title: Quantify genomic copy number standards
steps.instruction: Determine absolute genomic copy numbers of the slow‑growth pure cultures for later comparative analysis.

substeps.instruction: Use real‑time PCR or a spectroscopic method to measure absolute copy number.
Note that motile wild‑type Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 has ~60 genomes per cell in stationary phase.
Label the genome of the Synechocystis slow‑growth culture and apply inferential statistical analysis to generate a comparative genomic copy‑number reference for the mixed sample.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Capture 2D and 3D fluorescence data of mixed and pure cultures using LSM 510 microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Split the acquired channels.
Set intensity thresholds to enclose the majority of data points within a narrow range.
Extract quantitative values (mean intensity, geometric centre, binding area) directly from the original LSM 510 data.

steps.title: Compare fluorescence to pure controls
steps.instruction: Analyze mixed‑culture images against pure‑culture references.

substeps.instruction: Apply the same channel‑splitting and thresholding workflow to the mixed sample, the concurrently grown pure cultures, and the slow‑growth pure cultures.
Calculate the average fluorescence intensity (AFI) for each cell in the mixed culture.
Compare each cell’s AFI to the mean AFI of the corresponding pure‑culture control to differentiate species.

steps.title: Plot 3‑D cell data
steps.instruction: Visualize and compare spatial genomic information.

substeps.instruction: Plot the identified cells in 3‑D (x, y, z) using SigmaPlot 10.0 and compare with control plots.
Compare the genomic fluorescence area (GFA) of mixed‑culture cells with that of the slow‑growth pure‑culture standard to evaluate relative genomic copy number and assign each cell’s 3‑D locus.

steps.title: Validate species identification via autofluorescence
steps.instruction: Record the intrinsic autofluorescence of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 during imaging to confirm SAMI species discrimination.

substeps.instruction: Overlay the autofluorescent Synechocystis signal onto the mixed‑culture image to verify that Synechocystis cells are correctly distinguished from E. coli K‑12 MG1655.

description: In this assay, the autofluorescence of Synechocystis sp. strain PCC 6803 was concurrently recorded to verify the accuracy of SAMI in differentiating species. The autofluorescent image overlapped the outline of Synechocystis sp. strain PCC 6803 in the mixed culture, hence distinguishing them from E. coli K-12 MG1655. The autofluorescent overlaying images validated the accuracy of SAMI (Fig. 1(a) and (b)). The resulting 3D Images from the SAMI analyses are shown (Fig. 1(c) and (d)). The autofluorescence property of Synechocystis sp. Strain PCC 6803 was utilized to validate SAMI in this particular example. Autofluorescence was useful as a validating method for this particular example, but it is not a universal method applicable for any mixture of microorganisms. According to the statistical analysis, the sampling size was implied to be sufficient to represent the population, and therefore population size is equal to sampling size and population standard deviation is equal to sample standard deviation. A standardized variable [13] of 1.5 was used in setting up the relative standing of each population to obtain the optimal confidence interval as well as the confidence level between the species. The confidence level was 93.3% at a standardized variable of 1.5 from the statistic equations and the Z score Table [13]. The confidence interval of each species with different dyes was calculated. A 93% of accuracy was obtained in a case study of a two species mixed culture. The genomic copy number of slow growth pure culture can be analyzed by real time PCR method [14], [15] and it is well agreed with fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) analysis or radioactive labeling genome analysis [3].
